1) the FED is designed to operate in a radiation environment of 1 Mrad/year, and 2) the FED design is modular and scalable.

we have designed and simulated a VHDL model for the FED, and that we have designed a prototype board which is now under construction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the FED card and the associated firmware for the readout of the silicon strip tracker of the CMS experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider.
the design of a system that can process 3 GBytes of data in real-time, and is capable of being upgraded in the field to cope with higher data rates.

the following aspects: - the design of a 96 channel 10 bit ADC with 3.5 GBytes/s input data rate, - a 3 stage pipelined digital data processing chain, - a 10 bit 3 GBytes/ s data output link to the CMS data acquisition system.

the FPGA simulation tools are very powerful, but the user must understand how to make best use of the capabilities of these tools to obtain accurate results.
